description.value: The study examined immediate and delayed neural aftereffects of voluntary emotion regulation by detachment, focusing on amygdala activation during active regulation, the subsequent relaxation period, and later passive viewing.

spans.text: We explored whether there would be sustained downregulation or a postregulational, paradoxical increase of amygdala activation by studying the temporal dynamics of amygdala activation in two sequenced tasks.

design.value: A within-subject fMRI study of two sequenced tasks: an active emotion regulation task followed approximately ten minutes later by passive viewing of the same stimuli.

spans.text: The study was composed of two tasks.
Approximately ten minutes after end of task 1, we tested for a delayed aftereffect in task 2 (“passive viewing”).
